name: Grant Dawson
summary: A 33-year-old American Top Team lightweight (24-3-1 in our verified data) whose game is chain wrestling into back takes and rear-naked chokes. He is a slow burner: every UFC-era finish has come in round two or three, while all three of his career losses are first-round knockouts, the last two in the UFC (King Green in 33 seconds, Manuel Torres at 2:25). Comes off a come-from-behind third-round choke of Mateusz Rebecki at UFC 328.

how_they_fight.Striking: Functional rather than dangerous (about 3.6 significant strikes a minute at 52% accuracy). Uses kicks, including head kicks, to get reactions and set up level changes; he stunned Rebecki with an early head kick, but a caught head kick also got him tripped in round two. His hands are hittable when he stands in the pocket.
how_they_fight.Grappling: The engine of his game: about 3.1 takedowns per 15 minutes, 46% accuracy, and he owns roughly 59% of control time in his fights. Once on top he climbs to the back and hunts the rear-naked choke; he took Rebecki's back off a reversal in round one and again early in round three for the finish at 4:42. Controlled Diego Ferreira for over 10 minutes and Joe Solecki for almost 14 in decision wins.
how_they_fight.Defense: Takedown defense around 77%, but the striking defense (47%) is the hole. Knocked down by Rebecki's right hook in round two at UFC 328 and stopped in round one by Torres (dropped, then finished with ground strikes) and by King Green. When he loses, it is early and by strikes.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Classic slow burner who gets better as opponents tire. Verified UFC-era wins (13): zero in round one, four finishes in round two (Diaz, Trizano, Minner, Rafa Garcia), four in round three (Leonardo Santos at 4:59, Jared Gordon, Mark Madsen, Rebecki at 4:42) and five decisions. His last R1 finish was on the regional scene in 2016. All three losses (Hugh Pulley 2016, Green 2023, Torres 2025) are R1 KO/TKOs, so his danger zone is the first five minutes and his scoring zone is rounds two and three.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Patient and stubborn: after losing round two and being dropped by Rebecki he went straight back to grappling and found the finish late. He tends not to change course; if the takedown is not there he can drift into exchanges he should avoid.

patterns: Slow starter, late finisher: no R1 finish since 2016; 8 of his 13 UFC-era wins finished in R2-R3, the rest decisions
Wrestling to back control to rear-naked choke is the main finishing route (14 career submissions)
Uses kicks to draw reactions before level changes
Stays calm after adversity and goes back to his grappling
All three career losses are first-round KO/TKOs (Pulley 0:35, Green 0:33, Torres 2:25)
concerns: Chin and striking defense: dropped in each of his last two fights (Torres R1, Rebecki R2)
Aliev is himself a heavy wrestler (8 takedowns and over 12 minutes of control vs Mike Davis), so Dawson may not be able to choose where the fight happens
Weight-miss history: missed featherweight vs Darrick Minner (2020, 149.5 lb) and lightweight vs Mark Madsen (2022, 157.5 lb), per Wikipedia; no miss recorded since
Age 33 and a long career of hard weight cuts
keys_to_beat: Hurt him early: the first round is where he has been stopped every time
Stuff the first takedowns and make him strike in the pocket
Avoid giving up the back in scrambles, especially late when he is at his best
Win rounds with control time if the fight goes long; do not let him get a late round to chase the choke

news.text: Booked against unbeaten Nurullo Aliev on the UFC 333 prelims in Abu Dhabi; no injury or camp change reported. Still with American Top Team.
Submitted Mateusz Rebecki with a rear-naked choke at 4:42 of round three at UFC 328 after being knocked down in round two.
Stopped by Manuel Torres at 2:25 of round one at UFC 323 as a roughly 2-1 favourite, snapping a three-fight win streak.
